argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification claim than a bare unconditional launch approval. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.0 points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were observed, and the rollout starts at 6% with rollback capability, so deployment is operationally supportable. But the same admissible record also shows the logistics customs triage segment remains exposed, below target on tariff-code exception handling, and not covered by approved risk acceptance. The defensible position is therefore certification conditioned on explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of that exposed limitation, rather than certification on the theory that monitoring and rollback alone cure the governance gap.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalating this as if the record required outright rejection would impose launch delay despite admissible evidence that operational readiness and mitigation controls are materially present. The lower-cost policy-consistent path is to treat the issue as a disclosure condition on certification rather than as a basis for broader escalation, so long as the audit record makes that condition explicit.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is clear that rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. Here, the affected use case remains exposed and the draft risk acceptance is incomplete and does not address that exposure. On the admissible evidence, policy compliance is satisfied only in the narrower form: certification with explicit disclosure of the logistics customs triage limitation before launch.
concessions: The current record does not support a clean unconditional certification label.
The 6% rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring do not eliminate disclosure duties because the affected segment remains exposed.
The current risk acceptance draft is not approved and does not specifically cover the logistics customs triage exposure.
If explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure cannot be confirmed, the present admissible record does not establish full policy compliance for certification.
